key_agent_trends: Open-weight models advance for local agentic coding with Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Mini's looped architecture running on consumer hardware.
Voice agents become more practical and cheaper with OpenAI GPT-Live-1.1 API standby pricing and full-duplex improvements.
Autonomous agents demonstrate offensive security capabilities, finding and exploiting zero-days in minutes as shown in Amazon's MONAI Label report.
Decision models for routing, triage and guardrails improve with Baseten's Gemma 4-based open-weight releases topping benchmarks.
Agent deployment expands into browsers via Meta Muse Chrome sidebar while coding agents introduce new data-leak risks.

stories.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-Live-1.1 for voice agents in API, cuts idle cost to $0.02/min
stories.what_happened: On 19-20 November 2026 OpenAI made GPT-Live-1.1 available in the API as a full-duplex multilingual voice model. It improves accents, transcription of letters/numbers and task completion, can listen while speaking, and delegates deeper work to backend models. A new standby mode after idle timeout bills at $0.02 per minute versus $0.05 active. It previously powered ChatGPT voice.
stories.why_it_matters: Lower idle costs and better reliability make production voice agents more economical and natural for multi-turn tasks, accelerating agentic voice interfaces.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B looped open-weight model for local agentic coding
stories.what_happened: On 20 November 2026 Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, an Apache 2.0 open-weight MoE looped transformer with 26.4B total / 3.4B active parameters. Middle layers run three times per token for better reasoning at ~20GB footprint, runnable on 32GB Macs or DGX Spark. It leads sub-100B open models on DeepSWE and SWE-bench agentic coding benchmarks and supports 1M context with vision.
stories.why_it_matters: It brings high-quality local agentic coding and tool use to consumer hardware, reducing reliance on cloud frontier models for many workflows.

stories.headline: Amazon reports China-linked AI agents found and exploited MONAI Label zero-day in 11 minutes
stories.what_happened: Amazon Threat Intelligence disclosed on 20 November 2026 that autonomous agents using the open-source Cairn framework, given the goal 'obtain shell access', discovered a path-traversal zero-day in MONAI Label (CVE-2026-133968) and reached root on a university server in about 11 minutes. The September campaign targeted East Asian universities; no patched release yet. Authentication is off by default.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows autonomous agents can independently discover and weaponize zero-days at machine speed, raising the bar for defensive security and open-source software patching.

stories.headline: Baseten releases bison-1 and groundhog-1 open-weight decision models topping Decision Index
stories.what_happened: On 20 November 2026 Baseten released bison-1 (31B dense on Gemma 4) and groundhog-1 (26B MoE) open-weight decision models that return calibrated probabilities for yes/no, choice and score tasks. bison-1 ranks #1 on Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1 with 128k context and image support. Available on Baseten APIs and Hugging Face.
stories.why_it_matters: Specialized decision models improve routing, triage and guardrails for agent systems at lower cost and higher reliability than general LLMs.

stories.headline: Meta launches Muse AI agent in Chrome side panel extension, already used by 200k people
stories.what_happened: On 19-20 November 2026 Meta officially announced the Muse Chrome extension that places the Muse personal agent in the browser side panel. It can browse in the user's Chrome, act only in its own tab group, fill forms, compare prices and complete tasks, with approvals required. Meta says it cannot see passwords or history. Announced by Alexandr Wang after quiet testing.
stories.why_it_matters: It embeds a capable personal agent directly into the browser workflow, accelerating consumer adoption of agentic assistance for everyday tasks.

stories.headline: Together AI discloses prompt sample leak after AI coding agent committed private-repo credential
stories.what_happened: On 21 November 2026 Together AI disclosed that an unauthorized party downloaded stored prompt samples from June-July 2026 serverless inference requests after an AI coding agent committed a Hugging Face credential to the public xorl GitHub repo during development. Automated scanning reverted the commit, but the exposure window allowed the download. Samples from MiniMax, GLM and Kimi models were affected; some tested credentials were canaries.
stories.why_it_matters: It highlights risks of coding agents handling secrets and the data-retention practices of inference providers, prompting stronger defaults like zero data retention.

stories.headline: OpenAI says coding agents now complete 46% of multi-hour research tasks independently
stories.what_happened: In its 18 November 2026 report 'Research acceleration: The jagged frontier', OpenAI reported that coding agents complete an estimated 46% of two-to-four-hour research tasks without human help, up from 23% in March, and 35% of four-to-eight-hour tasks (from 13%). Success is uneven: 79% on monitoring training runs vs 25% on inference code. Median researcher daily agent spend reached ~$2,400.
stories.why_it_matters: It quantifies accelerating internal use of agents for AI research itself, showing jagged but rapid progress toward longer autonomous work while humans remain central.
